title: Music City at St. Luke’s Theatre #musiccity #musiccitymusical #countr...
transcript: Now in its encore production, Music City is back with a great cast and an immersive concert experience. It's set in the country music capital of Nashville, Tennessee, where dreams can weigh as heavily as sorrows, and a group of characters are struggling to catch a big break, or any break at all. The score is an eclectic group of hits by country songwriter JT Harding, superimposed onto a plot that has a little bit of everything — family tension, romance, and aching aspirations. Country music is a genre of contradictions — its lyricism is frequently trite yet specific, and it feels cliche yet heartfelt. This musical aptly holds this contradiction, somehow making its occasionally tropey story feel earnest in a way that works. The plot loses some steam in Act 2, but you're never far from a good song at any given moment. It’s a modestly sized cast with character doubling and multi-instrumentalists, but the intimate nature of the show by no means mutes the expansive musical performances. The music is the highlight here, and it sounds live and immediate, very much in and of the space it's being played in. If you're looking for a nontraditional musical experience, or you're in the mood to be transported out of New York for a couple hours, Music City is running at St. Luke's on 46th Street. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
